source: CARDI (Cambodian Agricultural Research and Development Institute) / វិទ្យាស្ថានស្រាវជ្រាវ និងអភិវឌ្ឍន៍កសិកម្មកម្ពុជា, presentation 'ផលិតកម្មគ្រាប់ពូជ គុណភាព និង ចំណាត់ថ្នាក់' (Seed Production, Quality, and Classification), prepared by Mr. Sang Laiyheng, Deputy Director of the Seed Multiplication Office (Tel: 012 952 801; Email: s_layheng@yahoo.com), dated December 1, 2014.
text:
CARDI's seed production system divides rice seed into five successive classes, each multiplied from the class above it:

1. Breeder Seed (BS) -- ក្រាប់ពូជសុទ្ធជម្រើសពូជវិទ្យា
2. Foundation Seed (FS) -- គ្រាប់ពូជគ្រឹះ
3. Registered Seed (RS) -- គ្រាប់ពូជទទួលស្គាល់
4. Certified Seed (CS) -- គ្រាប់ពូជអនុញ្ញាត
5. Graded Seed (GS) -- គ្រាប់ពូជល្អ

Regardless of which class is being produced, the training material stresses that every field practice must be carried out with the greatest care. In seed production fields, transplanting must be done in straight rows with only one seedling per hill (unlike ordinary rice production, where 2-3 seedlings per hill is normal), so that off-type plants are easy to spot and remove. Field care and maintenance must be done actively and consistently throughout the season in order to obtain good-quality seed and a high yield.

Foundation Seed is produced at dedicated seed multiplication stations, but Registered Seed and Certified Seed can be produced on farmers' fields, provided the fields are monitored and inspected by seed production technicians. Graded Seed is produced from Foundation Seed or from pure seed of other classes without strictly maintaining full seed-production isolation/inspection principles; its production follows practices similar to ordinary rice cultivation (transplanting 2-3 seedlings per hill), but all other seed-quality principles (cleanliness, rogueing, drying) must still be followed.
